correctness.rationale: Counting labeled-tree extensions of a fixed marked path gives A_(n,k)=(n-2)_(k-1)(k+1)n^(n-k-2). Deletion of a nonmarked leaf gives (n-k-1)q^(n-k-2) as total offpath expected leaves; marked endpoint deletion gives 2k/(k+1)q^(n-k-2). Their sum is (1); exact subtraction factorizes to (2), and strict increase of k(k+1)^2 proves every maximizer and tie. The root location is asymptotic to (2n)^(1/3); controlled q-expansion gives excess e^(-1). All boundaries n>=2 and k=n-1 were treated. Independent exact Prüfer enumeration of n<=7 and exact rational sign checks to n=300 produced 994 assertions. Finite tests are supplementary, not the universal proof.

value.rationale: The full-leaf statistic and fixed-pair distance are fundamental natural observables of uniform labeled trees. Exact conditional mean maximization reveals a nonmonotone dependence structure with a cube-root peak versus the classical square-root typical distance and infinitely many exact ties. This makes a mathematically motivated sharp extremal classification rather than an arbitrary finite parameter or routine marginal recomputation. The improvement in mean is correctly quantified as finite (e^(-1)), without exaggerating its extensive significance.
